title: Grant delays, customs reimbursements and health recovery fees
question: Did a late approval delay payment, cross a legal threshold or change what a contractor collected?
finding: San Francisco documented an invoicing delay. The customs agreement reached the Board before its tenth anniversary. Hospital collection fees varied by payer.
how: Compare signed authorities and staff chronology to dated transaction and expenditure records. Match contract numbers, grant scope and payer groups before totaling money.
limits: The sources cover different levels of government and time periods. A city-specific receipt and class-level billing records are still needed.

rows.test: Did the airport wait until its customs agreement had already crossed the ten-year threshold for Board approval?
rows.record: The November 2014 agreement had an indefinite term. Airport staff obtained Commission funding authorizations and brought it to the Board in July 2024, before its tenth anniversary. The analyst reported about $5.7 million in reimbursements. Two Controller contract numbers explicitly linked to AIR50020 account for $3,926,921.09. Earlier entries without a contract number cannot be assigned from the vendor name alone.
rows.limit: Request the crosswalk for the early purchase orders and the annual authorizations before reconciling the full amount.

rows.test: Did a three-month delay in workforce grant invoicing cause San Francisco to lose the award?
rows.record: On March 15, 2023, OEWD reported that it was three months behind schedule and unable to invoice. The Board authorized the $350,000 award on April 18. The regional June 2026 ledger reports $929,037 spent and $670,963 remaining on a $1.6 million award with a December 2026 end date. It does not break out San Francisco's receipts.

source.t: OEWD explanation of the invoicing delay

payment.t: Regional budget and expenditures, PDF page 4

rows.limit: Request city-specific invoices, approval dates, receipts and the disposition of any remaining city subaward.

rows.test: Did a retroactive health recovery contract charge a 20% fee on all reimbursements?
rows.record: Most work for Medi-Cal approval used fixed fees. The 20% rate applied to paid claims involving third-party payers. The analyst reported about $79.8 million in reimbursements recovered for DPH from July 2019 through December 2023. DPH documented contract negotiations and the February 2024 signature. The five-year forecast and contract ceiling describe future activity.

source.t: Analyst fee terms and recoveries, PDF page 5

rows.limit: Request aggregate recovery deposits by payer class and fixed-fee and contingent invoices for the same periods to test actual charges.
